title: European Commission — Digital Batteries Passport: data points by category
usedFor: The Commission's own data-point list for the battery passport, with per-category applicability and, per data point, the exact Annex/Article citation — the single most valuable gap-analysis input this register has produced.
licence: CC BY 4.0, confirmed 2026-08-11 directly from the document's own page 3: reuse authorised under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU, licensed CC BY 4.0, attribution required. No longer 'reported' — read verbatim.
source: https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/document/download/cd1e5e6c-4a4a-4b99-995a-49eb6916187e_en — fetched directly from the Commission's own site, not the third-party mirror. "Guidance Document: Digital Batteries Passport – data points by category", Version 1.0, 28 July 2026, DG GROW Directorate G Unit G2. Electronically signed 03/08/2026. A copy is retained in the project's internal reference archive; the download URL above is the citable source.
finding: Confirms the survey's prior IRI concern (Commission mints none) and resolves its metadata worry: 'v1.0 as of February 2027' was the survey's own conflation of the document's publish date (28 July 2026) with the *applicability* date it states inside (February 2027) — the primary document's own dating is internally consistent, nothing was actually wrong here once read directly. Covers EV, LMT and industrial batteries only (Art. 3 categories) — not portable or SLI. All 71 numbered data points read against `BatteryData` (`crates/dpp-domain/src/domain/sector/data/battery.rs`), each with its own Annex VI/XIII citation from the Commission itself. Confirmed matches: battery category, manufacturer identity (envelope-level), model ID, place/date of manufacture, weight, capacity, chemistry, critical raw materials, all four recycled-content percentages, expected lifetime in cycles, cathode/anode/electrolyte composition, and the entire Annex VII state-of-health parameter set (SOCE / remaining capacity / power capability / round-trip efficiency / self-discharge / ohmic resistance) — `StateOfHealth`'s two-variant design matches the Commission's own EV-vs-stationary/LMT split exactly. Gaps found here **triple-corroborate** the same gaps `batterypass-samm` and `catena-x-battery-pass` found independently, now each with the Commission's own citation: hazardous substances other than Hg/Cd/Pb (Annex VI A(8)) — nothing analogous to `SvhcSubstance`; usable extinguishing agent (Annex VI A(9)); share of renewable content (Annex XIII 1(f)) — distinct from recycled content, wholly absent; minimum and maximum voltage (Annex XIII 1(h)) — only nominal voltage is modelled; original power capability and power limits (Annex XIII 1(i)) — no power field exists at all; reference test used for expected lifetime (Annex XIII 1(j)); capacity threshold for exhaustion (Annex XIII 1(k)); commercial warranty period (Annex XIII 1(m)); C-rate of the cycle-life test (Annex XIII 1(p)); Art. 13(4)/13(5) marking requirements (Annex XIII 1(q)); EU declaration of conformity reference (Annex XIII 1(r)); waste-battery prevention/management info per Art. 74(1)(a)-(f) (Annex XIII 1(s)); part numbers and spare-parts sourcing contacts (Annex XIII 2(b)); safety measures (Annex XIII 2(d)); test-report results proving compliance (Annex XIII 3); capacity/power/round-trip-efficiency fade and internal-resistance increase, all four as dynamic (individual-battery, not model-level) figures (Annex XIII 4(a)); expected lifetime in calendar years, distinct from cycles (Annex XIII 4(a)); battery status — original/repurposed/re-used/remanufactured/waste (Annex XIII 4(c)); and periodic charge-cycle/state-of-charge/negative-event recording (Annex XIII 4(d)), of which `HarmfulEvents` only partially covers. Two items are correctly *not* gaps: the carbon footprint declaration/label (Annex XIII 1(c)) is explicitly 'not to be filled/displayed as of February 2027 — format still to be specified in the upcoming implementing act', matching our own correctly-blocked CFB stub; likewise the printable-instructions requirement (Annex XIII 1(t)) is on hold pending Omnibus IV.
nextStep: This document supplies the citation every one of the 20 gaps above needs — no further primary-text search is required for most of them, only deciding field shape and schema version. Sequence by what the Commission marks Mandatory-now for the most categories first: hazardous substances, renewable content, min/max voltage, power, warranty period, C-rate, marking/conformity-declaration references, and waste-battery info are all Mandatory today for at least EV and LMT. The dynamic/individual-battery vs. static/model-level distinction (Annex XIII point 4 vs. points 1-3) is architectural, not a field list — `BatteryData` does not currently distinguish declared model-level figures from measured individual-battery ones the way `StateOfHealth`/`ExpectedLifetime` already do for state-of-health; the new fade/resistance-increase/cycle-count fields belong in that same disclosure-gated, per-battery shape, not as flat `BatteryData` additions.
